identity_and_session.conflict_declaration: This producer session does not independently review or accept ENG-200 and cannot decide GATE-001.
identity_and_session.forbidden_context_attestation: No HOLDOUT or REPLICATION content was accessed. The prototype uses synthetic TRAIN/DEV-only routing cases and contains no confirmatory outcome data.

scientific_decisions.M19: Executed Teacher Router: a deterministic runtime executes the frozen canonical routing policy before Qwen; Qwen does not select the capability.
scientific_decisions.M20: Explained Teacher Router: Qwen receives the frozen policy explanation plus typed neutral capability catalogue and selects an opaque capability handle.
scientific_decisions.tree_vs_prolog: The SWI-Prolog router is deterministically lowered from the same canonical IR. Tree-versus-Prolog is an engineering representation/runtime comparison, not an independent semantic treatment and not a Qwen-effect claim when downstream inputs are identical.
scientific_decisions.capability_identity: Policy nodes reference canonical internal capability IDs. Qwen-visible catalogues expose opaque handles; canonical IDs are hidden from Qwen.
scientific_decisions.schema_surface: Neutral labels/descriptions are the primary M20 surface. Schema-adapted labels/descriptions are a separate DEV-only treatment factor under identical canonical IDs, handles, versions and semantics.
scientific_decisions.router_scope: The router selects capabilities only. It does not compute epistemic status, action, conclusion, SQL rows, Prolog proofs, Python results or final answers.
scientific_decisions.prototype_teacher_status: The committed policy is a producer-authored synthetic contract exemplar. It is not represented as an empirical Codex-generated policy and cannot by itself support a teacher-effect claim.
scientific_decisions.confirmatory_status: M19/M20 and representation/schema ablations remain DEV-first proposals until WP-004, WP-006 and WP-007 independently adjudicate a powered feasible subset before HOLDOUT.

producer_findings: The first CI attempt correctly failed because YAML inline mapping syntax truncated comma-containing Qwen-visible descriptions; the registry was corrected to explicit mappings and deterministic regeneration subsequently passed.
A single canonical IR can drive both decision-graph and Prolog routing without duplicating normative policy rules.
Schema/name adaptation can be isolated from routing policy by preserving canonical IDs, opaque handles, versions and capability semantics byte-for-byte at the identity layer.
known_limitations: No actual Qwen routing/model run is part of this producer package; M19/M20 behavioral effects remain unmeasured.
No empirical Codex-generated routing-policy candidate has been produced or selected; the committed policy is a synthetic contract exemplar only.
The required direct-Qwen capability-selection baseline and simple human/static SOP router are defined but not empirically executed in this package.
The neutral-versus-schema-adapted catalogue ablation has contract evidence only and has not yet been evaluated with Qwen.
Teacher-generation token/time, Qwen catalogue/policy token counts, tree/Prolog latency, annotation cost and routing failure rates remain WP-006/WP-007 inputs to measure before confirmatory inclusion.
Unrelated repository workflows may fail on later HEADs because of their own attestation assumptions; only the named ENG-200 workflow/run is producer evidence for this package.
